known_incidents.summary: At MinerU local VLM API concurrency 3, 48 of 54 pages failed with a tensor-shape mismatch in concurrent VLM inference. The set of pages that succeeded changed between repeats, so no accuracy metric was computed and the candidate was not promotion-eligible. Empty artifacts were recorded as failures, never as successful blank pages.
known_incidents.standing_rule: concurrency per worker = 1; throughput scales by horizontal replicas only. 8 workers x concurrency 1, never 1 worker x concurrency 8.

known_incidents.summary: The local VLM engine only passed its one-image smoke test after the declared optional dependency accelerate>=1.5.1 was supplied as the pinned version 1.14.0.
known_incidents.standing_rule: accelerate is pinned to 1.14.0, not left as a range.

historical_evidence.full_campaign: This runtime plus the FOLYNTA/TAVONEL recovery runtime produced 5,131 of 5,132 outputs = 99.98% completion. That is completion, not accuracy.

to_verify_in_canary: Which engine `vlm-engine` resolves to - the single most important line in the receipt. MinerU calls get_vlm_engine(inference_engine='auto') and picks vllm-engine when vllm is importable, transformers otherwise. The base image DOES ship vllm, so the adapter reads the resolved engine and fails closed with MODEL_LOAD unless it equals inference_config.expected_vlm_engine. If the canary shows vllm-engine being chosen, that is a finding and a founder decision: pin the transformers engine (matching the 2026-08 c1 evidence) or re-baseline on vllm-engine and say so in the report. It is never silently accepted.
batch_size=1 is passed explicitly rather than leaving MinerU's set_default_batch_size() to choose; confirm the loaded client reports 1.

No TENSOR_SHAPE failures at concurrency 1 across the 15 canary pages, and byte-identical output on a repeat of the same page. Any TENSOR_SHAPE at concurrency 1 is a stop-the-line finding, not a retry.
Per-page latency against the 34.708 s/page historical figure. shard_size_hint is 100 and the scheduler must start this model's shards first (masterplan section 35) because it is the slowest lane.
Record importlib.metadata.version('mineru') and the git sha - expect 3.4.4 and fbb1257a, per upstream_version_discrepancy above.
Peak VRAM on A40 and on RTX 4090, since gpu_pool_priority prefers A40.
gpu_pool_priority entries are RunPod gpuTypeId strings taken from masterplan section 13.3; confirm each against the provider catalog snapshot.

framework_floor_audit.required: MinerU 3.4.5 pyproject [vlm] extra: transformers >= 4.57.3, < 5.0.0, accelerate >= 1.5.1, torch >= 2.6.0, < 3. That floor also covers the checkpoint's own declared transformers_version 4.57.2.
framework_floor_audit.image_ships: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.21.0 - transformers version unknown from evidence (the tag's requirements/common.txt bounds transformers >= 4.56.0, < 5). The vLLM server is not used: MinerU's vlm-engine resolves to the in-process transformers engine (ARENA_CONTRACT 11.6).
framework_floor_audit.action: no pin change - transformers==4.57.3 is already installed exactly. bootstrap.sh gains an architecture preflight that checks model_type qwen2_vl against transformers' CONFIG_MAPPING_NAMES, builds the config with AutoConfig, and fails closed unless MinerU's vlm-engine resolves to the pinned transformers engine.
framework_floor_audit.superseded_by: d59_vlm_engine_correction (the 'vLLM server is not used ... resolves to the in-process transformers engine' sentence above was the wrong resolution of the to_verify_in_canary item above it; the transformers-version floor conclusion stays correct because vllm-engine still needs transformers to build the checkpoint's AutoConfig)

d59_vlm_engine_correction.finding: Real canary pod plz5obsz7ega3a (A40) hit the to_verify_in_canary item above head-on: MinerU logged 'Using vllm-engine as the inference engine for VLM' and bootstrap.sh's architecture preflight raised '[arena] FATAL architecture preflight: MinerU's vlm-engine resolved to 'vllm-engine', but runtime.json's inference_config.expected_vlm_engine is 'transformers''.
d59_vlm_engine_correction.decision: Re-baseline on vllm-engine, not pin transformers. adapter.py and bootstrap.sh both call get_vlm_engine(inference_engine='auto', is_async=False) with no explicit backend override, so the auto-detected engine is what actually runs; mineru/utils/engine_utils.py's _select_linux_engine always returns 'vllm' (formatted 'vllm-engine') when `import vllm` succeeds, and it always succeeds on this runtime's base image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.21.0. That is not a defect to work around: MinerU's own docker/global/Dockerfile also FROMs vllm/vllm-openai:v0.21.0, and model_registry.json's official_inference_config for mineru_vlm (resolved from the model card, independent of this bug) already names backend 'vllm-engine'.
d59_vlm_engine_correction.unchanged: The in-process claim (no HTTP model server) still holds under vllm-engine: mineru/backend/vlm/vlm_analyze.py's ModelSingleton.get_model holds it as an in-process vllm.LLM object, not a server - that is the separate 'http-client' backend - so ARENA_CONTRACT 11.6 and entrypoint.sh's `exec` (D19) are unaffected.

cuda_floor.vendor_documented_floor: none published: the vendor documents no driver floor beyond the image's own CUDA runtime
cuda_floor.capacity_note: 13.0 is the newest CUDA version RunPod filters on, so allowedCudaVersions is the single entry ["13.0"]. A capacity refusal for this model is a real refusal, not a placement that could be widened.
cuda_floor.rationale: min_cuda_version is the lowest CUDA version a RunPod host may report for this runtime to start. It is sent as the create payload's allowedCudaVersions -- every version RunPod lists at or above it -- because pod 3xag0y00rgoj4n ran this campaign's CUDA 12.9 image on a host reporting cudaVersion 12.8 and died in torch._C._cuda_init with CUDA error 804 after the pod was already billing. Read anonymously from the pinned image's own OCI config blob at the digest runtime.json pins; nothing is inferred from the image name.
